headline: Graphify gives AI coding agents a map of your codebase, improving navigation and efficiency
summary: Graphify is an open-source CLI that creates a knowledge graph of your code, helping AI agents understand connections instead of aimlessly searching.
details: Graphify is an open-source CLI tool that transforms your codebase into a local knowledge graph. This helps AI coding agents navigate complex repositories by understanding the actual relationships between files, functions, and concepts.

Traditional AI agents often struggle with large codebases, getting stuck in cycles of searching and reopening files. Graphify provides a 'map' where code elements are nodes and dependencies (calls, imports) are edges, allowing agents to jump to the right place and follow connections.

Installation is straightforward using uv, pipx, or pip, requiring Python 3.10 or later. Graphify integrates with popular tools like Copilot in VS Code and Copilot CLI, or can be used directly from the terminal to build a code graph.

After mapping, users can explore an interactive graph.html and a GRAPH_REPORT.md for a comprehensive project overview. The tool provides context as nodes, relations, and file references, with a default budget of 2000 tokens for results.

AI agents can directly query the graph, asking specific questions like "using the graph, what depends on the auth module?". Graphify transparently tags each edge as EXTRACTED, INFERRED, or AMBIGUOUS, indicating the parsing confidence.

For agents to call the graph tools directly, users can install the MCP extra and register it with an absolute path to the graph. This enables agents to utilize functions such as graph_stats and query_graph for deeper insights.

Users are encouraged to compare agent performance with and without Graphify by posing complex questions, like "where is user input validated before it hits the database?". This comparison effectively demonstrates the tool's efficiency in reducing redundant file access.
Full documentation is available at docs.graphify.com. As an open-source project, a star on GitHub helps other developers discover Graphify if it proves useful for your workflow.
